verdicts.text: Env zero (env0) prices its paid tiers per successful apply or environment.

verdicts.text: Spacelift's paid plans scale by private worker count rather than seats or resources, with quote-based pricing at the top end.
verdicts.evidence: Spacelift's pricing page describes every paid tier as having unlimited users, with tiers set apart by how many workers they include: "The Enterprise plan is offered as an annual subscription and includes unlimited users and 5 to 30 private workers." Business and above are priced by quote. Spacelift's own blog also says pricing "centers on your plan and worker capacity (public or private)... instead of paying per resource."
verdicts.framing_note: The sources say tiers are unlimited-user and set apart by worker count, with quotes for Business, Enterprise and Enterprise+ ("priced on request" per Scalr). Starter+ also includes public workers and has a listed price of $20k/yr, so "scale by private worker count" is a slight simplification.

verdicts.text: Cloud-native tools like AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Azure ARM, Azure Bicep, and Google Cloud Infrastructure Manager carry no separate tool fee; open-source tools OpenTofu, Kubernetes, and Crossplane are free to run.
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass1) Google's Infrastructure Manager pricing page lists no fee for the service itself. It says "Infrastructure Manager charges for Cloud Build execution and Cloud Storage storage", which are the underlying services it uses, so "no separate tool fee" holds. It is well known that AWS CDK, CloudFormation (for AWS-native resources), ARM, and Bicep are free, and that OpenTofu, Kubernetes, and Crossplane are open source.
verdicts.intuition_flag: CloudFormation bills for third-party extension/hook handler operations. Kubernetes and Crossplane are free to license, but the clusters they run on cost money, so "free to run" is loose wording.
